title: Reduced singleton-image maps factor through a field monomorphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X,Y$ algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], $F$ a field [def-weil-field], and $j:\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$ a quasi-compact monomorphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Here monomorphism means injectivity of composition with $j$ on morphisms from every algebraic space over $S$, and quasi-compact means that after every scheme test inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Let $x$ be the unique point in the image of $j$, with point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. If $Y$ is reduced (the rings of sections on affine opens of an etale scheme atlas have no nonzero nilpotents) and $f:Y\to X$ has point image contained in $\{x\}$, there is a unique $S$-morphism $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ with $j\circ g=f$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $X$ or $Y$.

source.place: Tags 0H1T (lemma-factor-through-residual-space-decent) and 0H1R (lemma-residual-space-monomorphism); uniqueness follows from the monomorphism hypothesis.

proof.text: Choose an affine component $A$ of the atlas in [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] with a point over $x$. Its etale image $E\subseteq X$ is open and quasi-compact, and admits a quasi-compact scheme atlas, by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], both $f$ and $j$ factor through $E$. The induced $j_E:\operatorname{Spec}F\to E$ remains quasi-compact: for every scheme $H\to E$, its pullback is exactly $H\times_X\operatorname{Spec}F$ by the comparison in that node. It remains monomorphic by cancellation with $E\hookrightarrow X$.

source.place: Tag 0H1T, shrinking to a quasi-compact open neighbourhood.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-qc-space-schematic-strata] to $E$ and $j_E$. Obtain an open $U\subseteq E$ and a closed subspace $T\hookrightarrow U$ represented by a scheme, whose point image contains $x$. Both $f$ and $j$ factor through $U$ by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. Choose a reduced scheme atlas $w:W\to Y$ as in the reducedness hypothesis; its affine section rings are reduced, so $W$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The pullback $P=W\times_U T\to W$ is a closed immersion of schemes by the closed-subspace convention in [lem-sfb-qc-space-schematic-strata]. Its point image is all of $|W|$ by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], since $f w$ maps into $\{x\}\subseteq|T|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme], the identity of $W$ factors through $P$. Projecting gives $b:W\to T$ with composite $f w$. The same argument with the reduced scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$ in place of $W$ gives $j_T:\operatorname{Spec}F\to T$ with composite $j$.

source.place: Tag 0H1T, schematic stratum and reduced-source factorization; uses schemes.tex Tag 0356 after an atlas instead of appealing to spaces-properties.tex Tag 03JJ without a node.

proof.text: The map $T\to X$ is injective on points: the closed-subspace clause of [lem-sfb-qc-space-schematic-strata] identifies $|T|$ with a subset of $|U|$, and the open inclusions identify $|U|$ with a subset of $|X|$ by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Let $t$ be the image of $j_T$. Thus $b(|W|)\subseteq\{t\}$. The map $j_T$ is a monomorphism of schemes: equality after $j_T$ implies equality after $j$, hence equality by the hypothesis on $j$. For arbitrary scheme tests the equality induces the same $S$-structure on the test, so that this cancellation applies to $S$-morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0H1T, reduction to the one-point scheme problem.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], $j_T=i_t\circ a$ for a morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. Because $j_T$ is monomorphic, $a$ is monomorphic: if $a u=a v$, compose with $i_t$ and cancel $j_T$. Apply [lem-sfb-monomorphism-into-field-coproduct] to the one-element family with field $\kappa(t)$. The subset of components cannot be empty because $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is nonempty; hence $a$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-scheme-single-point-residue-factorization] to $b:W\to T$: reducedness of $W$ and the singleton-image condition were checked above. It gives $h:W\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ with $i_t h=b$. Set $g_W=a^{-1}h$. Then $j_Tg_W=b$ and $jg_W=fw$. All maps are over $S$: $T\to S$ induces the structure on its residue-field spectrum, and composing $j_T=i_ta$ with $T\to S$ shows $a$ is over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0H1T, final reduction to morphisms.tex Tag 0H1M; schemes.tex Tag 03DP identifies the given field with the scheme residue field.

proof.text: For every scheme test $H\to Y$, the pullback $W_H\to H$ is a surjective etale map of schemes by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. It is an fppf covering by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-pc-fppf-site]. The restriction of $g_W$ to $W_H$ has equal pullbacks to $W_H\times_H W_H$: their composites with $j$ both equal the restriction of $f$, and $j$ is monomorphic. The fppf sheaf condition for the algebraic space $\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] gives a unique map $g_H:H\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. The equality $jg_H=f|_H$ holds after the same cover, hence holds by the sheaf condition for $X$. For $H'\to H$ over $Y$, the maps $g_{H'}$ and $g_H|_{H'}$ have equal composites with $j$, so are equal. The $g_H$ therefore define a natural transformation $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, with $jg=f$. Any two such $g$ are equal by the stated monomorphism hypothesis. This also covers empty $Y$, since the sheaf condition on the empty covering gives the unique sections on empty tests.
